- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥0.67) and forecast is above recent mean, reduce forecast slightly to avoid overreaction.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤0.33) and forecast is below recent mean, increase forecast modestly to avoid underreaction.  
- If forecast spikes sharply after a recent spike in sentiment, apply a lag correction: reduce forecast by 5–10% for the next 3–5 periods.  
- If forecast mean reverts too aggressively after a strong move, adjust by adding 1–2% of the recent 7-day average to prevent premature correction.  
- For 30-day forecasts, if sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.33–0.67), use a 3-period moving average of recent prices to anchor forecast, avoiding sentiment-driven extremes.  
- If sentiment history shows repeated 1–2 day reversals, apply a smoothing filter to reduce forecast volatility beyond 3–5 periods.
